Wat is FinOps? Uitleg, definitie en de F: What is FinOps? Explanation, definition and the FinOps Lifecycle | AX1S Infra
{1}FinOps{/1} brengt finance, engineerin: {1}FinOps{/1} brings finance, engineering and operations together to reduce waste in cloud, SaaS and AI spend and to get more value out of technology. It is not a one-off action but a continuous practice in which every team takes ownership of its own costs and usage.
De FinOps Foundation, onderdeel van de L: The FinOps Foundation, part of the Linux Foundation, is the non-profit organisation behind this practice. It develops the FinOps framework, the annual State of FinOps benchmark and the FinOps Certified Practitioner certification.
De FinOps Lifecycle: Inform, Optimize, O: The FinOps Lifecycle: Inform, Optimize, Operate
Het FinOps-framework beschrijft een door: The FinOps framework describes a continuous cycle of three phases, which is gone through again and again as cloud, SaaS and AI usage changes:
{1}{2}{3}Inform:{/3} zichtbaarheid creër: {1}{2}{3}Inform:{/3} create visibility into who spends what, with correct tagging, allocation and benchmarking, so teams can see their own costs.{/2}
{1}{2}{3}Optimize:{/3} op basis van die: {1}{2}{3}Optimize:{/3} on the basis of that visibility, save in a targeted way: rightsizing, commitments such as Reserved Instances or Savings Plans, and cleaning up unused resources.{/2}
{1}{2}{3}Operate:{/3} optimalisatie borg: {1}{2}{3}Operate:{/3} embed optimisation in processes and automation, so cost management doesn't stay a one-off project but becomes part of how teams work.{/2}
FinOps is per definitie cross-functionee: FinOps is cross-functional by definition. Finance brings budget discipline and forecasting, engineering knows the technical options for optimisation, and business/product teams understand which spend creates value. Without these three at the table together, cost management ends up either too technical or too far removed from practice.
Waarin verschilt FinOps van traditioneel: How does FinOps differ from traditional cost management?
Traditioneel kostenbeheer is periodiek e: Traditional cost management is periodic and top-down: an annual budget, checked after the fact by finance. FinOps is continuous and decentralised: teams see their own usage in (near) real time and make decisions themselves, within a shared framework. That fits the nature of cloud, SaaS and AI spend, which can fluctuate per hour or even per API call, unlike the fixed infrastructure costs of the past.
Hoe begin je met FinOps?: How do you get started with FinOps?
De meeste organisaties starten met zicht: Most organisations start with visibility: knowing who spends what, before optimising. Where an organisation currently stands often differs per practice (cost allocation, optimisation, planning) and doesn't need to be the same everywhere. In {1}the FinOps maturity model{/1} you can read how to determine that for your organisation, and {2}5 ways to eliminate unnecessary cloud costs{/2} lists concrete first steps.
Een engineeringteam draait een testomgev: An engineering team runs a test environment on heavy instance types because nobody knows exactly which capacity is needed. Without FinOps, finance only sees at the end of the quarter that cloud costs have risen, without knowing why. With FinOps the team sees the usage itself, recognises the overprovisioning within a few weeks and adjusts the instance types based on actual usage. The same logic applies to SaaS subscriptions nobody uses any more and AI workloads whose cost per API call keeps rising: visibility at the team itself is what makes the difference.

Het beheersen van uitgaven aan AI- en LL: Controlling spend on AI and LLM workloads: compute for training and inference, API costs from model providers, and data storage. Because of the rapid growth and variable usage patterns of AI workloads, this is one of the fastest-growing focus areas within FinOps.
Twee manieren om cloudkosten zichtbaar t: Two ways of making cloud costs visible per team or product. With showback you see the costs but they aren't actually charged; with chargeback the amount is really allocated to the team's budget. Showback is often the first step towards chargeback.
Overkoepelende term voor het financieel: Umbrella term for the financial management of cloud spend, of which FinOps is the most common practice. Besides optimisation, CFM also covers budgeting, forecasting and governance.
De kosten van cloud-infrastructuur uitge: The cost of cloud infrastructure expressed per unit of value, for example per customer, per transaction or per API call. This shows whether technology costs grow along with revenue or rise faster: an important signal for CFOs.
Cloud-capaciteit waarvoor wordt betaald: Cloud capacity that is paid for but no longer (or never) used usefully: forgotten test environments, unused storage volumes, oversized instances. Often the first and fastest source of savings in a FinOps engagement. See also our {1}5 ways to eliminate unnecessary cloud costs{/1}.
Verzamelnaam voor kortingen die je krijg: Collective name for discounts you get in exchange for a usage or spend commitment to a cloud provider, such as Reserved Instances and Savings Plans. The longer and more certain the commitment, the higher the discount generally is. Work it out yourself with our {1}RI vs. Savings Plan Calculator{/1}.
Het proces waarbij cloud-, SaaS- en AI-k: The process of assigning cloud, SaaS and AI costs to the teams, products or cost centres that cause them. Requires consistent tagging and is the foundation for both showback and chargeback.
Het automatisch signaleren van onverwach: Automatically flagging unexpected cost spikes, for example caused by a misconfigured resource or a forgotten process that keeps running. Early detection prevents a mistake from running for weeks before anyone notices.
Een certificering van de FinOps Foundati: A certification from the FinOps Foundation that demonstrates someone understands and can apply the FinOps framework. Both founders of AX1S Infra are FinOps Certified Practitioners.
De non-profit organisatie achter het Fin: The non-profit organisation behind the FinOps framework, part of the Linux Foundation. It publishes, among other things, the annual State of FinOps benchmark and manages the FinOps Certified Practitioner certification.
De drie doorlopende fasen van het FinOps: The three continuous phases of the FinOps framework: Inform (create visibility), Optimize (save in a targeted way) and Operate (embed optimisation in processes). See {1}What is FinOps?{/1} for the full explanation.
Het consistent beheren van kosten, toega: Consistently managing costs, access and policy across multiple cloud providers. Without governance, different tagging standards, security levels and reporting methods quickly emerge per cloud. More on this in {1}Multi-cloud governance without the complexity{/1}.
Een commitment aan een specifiek instanc: A commitment to a specific instance type in a specific region, generally for 1 or 3 years, in exchange for a substantial discount compared with on-demand rates. Less flexible than a Savings Plan, but often with a slightly higher discount. Compare both options with our {1}RI vs. Savings Plan Calculator{/1}.
Het aanpassen van de capaciteit van een: Adjusting the capacity of a resource (e.g. a virtual machine) to actual usage. Oversized instances are one of the most common forms of cloud waste.
De ongecontroleerde groei van SaaS-abonn: The uncontrolled growth of SaaS subscriptions within an organisation, often purchased by individual teams without central oversight. Leads to duplicate tools, forgotten licences and unnecessary costs.
Een commitment op een vast bedrag aan co: A commitment to a fixed amount of compute spend per hour, for 1 or 3 years, regardless of instance type or region. More flexible than a Reserved Instance, with a comparable (sometimes slightly lower) discount. Compare both with our {1}RI vs. Savings Plan Calculator{/1} or read the background in {2}Reserved Instances vs. Savings Plans{/2}.
Ongebruikte cloudcapaciteit die tegen ee: Unused cloud capacity offered at a heavily reduced rate, with the risk that the capacity can be reclaimed at short notice. Suitable for interruptible workloads such as batch processing.
Het labelen van cloud-resources met meta: Labelling cloud resources with metadata such as team, project or environment. The basis for reliable cost allocation: without consistent tagging, accurate reporting per team is almost impossible.
De volledige kosten van een technologiek: The full cost of a technology choice over its entire lifetime, including not only the direct cloud or licence costs but also management, migration and any decommissioning.

5 kostbare fouten die je public cloud on: 5 costly mistakes that make your public cloud needlessly expensive | AX1S Infra
Het zit in architectuur, capaciteit en c: It lies in architecture, capacity and contracts that no longer match how something is actually used. That makes these mistakes harder to find than an isolated misconfiguration, but they are the pattern we see most often at AX1S in cloud bills that come in far higher than necessary. These are the five that most often carry through into the bill.
1. Je rekent alleen met het gebruik van: 1. You only calculate with today's usage
Wat gebeurt er met de kosten als het aan: What happens to costs if the number of users, transactions or the amount of data doubles? Anyone who doesn't ask that question upfront is confronted with it at the first growth spurt. So calculate in advance with several scenarios: normal usage, growth and peak load, so the architecture works not just for today.
Ongebruikte capaciteit kost ook geld, oo: Unused capacity costs money too, even when nothing runs on it. So look at actual usage and, where possible, make sure capacity can scale up and down automatically, instead of sizing well above need by default.
3. Je gaat te vroeg langdurige verplicht: 3. You commit to long-term obligations too early
Reserved Instances en Savings Plans kunn: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans can deliver a lot of benefit, but only if you actually use the capacity. So only commit once usage is predictable enough. (Not sure which form suits you? Read our article on {1}Reserved Instances vs. Savings Plans{/1}, or calculate it directly with our {2}RI vs. Savings Plan Calculator{/2}.)
Een cloudomgeving bestaat uit meer dan s: A cloud environment consists of more than servers. Storage, databases, backups, networking, logging and managed services often weigh at least as heavily in the total bill. So look at the cost of the entire workload, not just its most visible component.
5. Je kijkt pas naar kosten als de omgev: 5. You only look at costs once the environment is already running
Dan kun je nog steeds optimaliseren, maa: You can still optimise then, but important choices have often already been made. So include costs during the design phase. Not only: does this architecture work technically? But also: what does this architecture cost at growth and over the full period of use?
Dat is waar FinOps volgens AX1S meer om: That is what FinOps is more about, according to AX1S: not just saving afterwards, but making better choices upfront. (Is your environment already running and do you want to clean up first? Also read our article on {1}5 ways to eliminate unnecessary cloud costs{/1}.)

5 manieren om onnodige cloudkosten te el: 5 ways to eliminate unnecessary cloud costs | AX1S Infra
Cloudkosten groeien zelden door één grot: Cloud costs rarely grow because of one big mistake. They build up through a pile of small decisions: a test environment that keeps running after the sprint, a storage volume that was never cleaned up, an instance chosen two sizes too big "just to be sure". Harmless on their own, but together they quickly add up to tens of percent of unnecessary spend.
De goede kant van het verhaal: al deze b: The good news: all these sources of waste can be recognised and fixed without it costing performance or agility. Below are the five places where we most often find immediate savings at customers.
Je kunt niet besparen op wat je niet zie: You can't save on what you can't see. The first step is always a baseline: which resources are running, who created them, and what are they actually used for? A good tagging strategy is indispensable here: without consistent tags for team, project and environment, cost analysis stays guesswork.
This is almost always the quickest win. Examples we come across structurally:
{1} Losgekoppelde opslagvolumes die nooi: {1} Detached storage volumes that were never deleted after a server was torn down
{1} Snapshots en back-ups die veel lange: {1} Snapshots and backups retained far longer than policy prescribes
{1} Load balancers en IP-adressen zonder: {1} Load balancers and IP addresses without active traffic
{1} Test- en staging-omgevingen die na k: {1} Test and staging environments that simply keep running after office hours
3. Rightsizing: betaal voor wat je nodig: 3. Rightsizing: pay for what you need
Instances worden vaak overgedimensioneer: Instances are often oversized at the start of a project and never reconsidered afterwards. By analysing usage data over a few weeks, you can systematically determine the right instance size, often with 20 to 40 percent savings on the workload concerned, without any impact on performance.
Voor voorspelbare, continue workloads li: For predictable, continuous workloads, substantial discounts are waiting via Reserved Instances or Savings Plans. The trick is to commit only on the part of your usage that is structural, and to leave variable or uncertain workloads on on-demand. (You can read more about this in our article on {1}Reserved Instances vs. Savings Plans{/1}.)
Zodra teams zelf zien wat hun infrastruc: As soon as teams see for themselves what their infrastructure costs, behaviour changes on its own. Cost allocation per team or product isn't meant to punish, but to create ownership. After all, the most sustainable form of saving is the one that doesn't have to be enforced again and again.
Uit onze eigen trajecten blijkt dat deze: Our own engagements show that these five steps together are generally good for an average saving of 23% on cloud and compute spend, without compromising scalability.
